source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 10 мая ст. ст. — «Мч. Исихия Антиохийского (IV).»

attestations.note: **This row is a reading the author should check, and it is written here rather than as a second folder because a duplicate is the worse error.** BRIEF.md §3.4 decides it: a line on the same menologion day under the same name is that man, and the Romanian «Sfântul Cuvios Isihie Mărturisitorul» and the Greek «Όσιος Ησύχιος ο Ομολογητής» this folder already stands on are both the 10 May Hesychius, as is the Russian «Мч. Исихия Антиохийского». **What does not agree is the rank.** The Romanian and Greek call him venerable and confessor; the Russian calls him мученик, a martyr, and gives the martyrdom in full — a man of high and honoured office at the imperial court at Antioch under Максимиан Галерий (305–311), stripped of a dignitary’s dress by the edict that put Christians out of military rank, set among the women’s servants, and drowned in the river with a millstone about his neck. Confessor and martyr are not in conflict over such a death, and the disgrace before the drowning is what a confessor’s title would rest on; but **`types` was NOT touched** and stays `venerable` and `confessor`, because changing a rank on a contested identification is more than this row claims. `dates` was not touched either: the folder has none, the Russian day line gives «(IV)», the fourth century, and the life says in its own last sentence «Год смерти мученика точно не известен», the year of the martyr’s death is not exactly known — which is a refusal of a year and not a year. The folder’s own life already says the Greek page for 10 May sends the reader to 6 March for his life and that a separate martyr Hesychius stands on the Greek 2 September as `hesychius-the-martyr-2-september`; neither page was read here. The corpus’s twelve Hesychius folders were listed and read against this line before the row was written: none is of Antioch, and the nearest in dossier is `hesychius-the-senator`, a martyr the Romanian and Greek keep on 2 March whose epithet would fit a man of the imperial court — a different day in both calendars, and nothing read links them. `fk.mjs` on «Исихий Антиохийский» returned NONE. azbyka.ru was not read, and it is a source that might settle the rank.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 10 mai — «Sfântul Cuvios Isihie Mărturisitorul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Ησύχιος ο Ομολογητής»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 10 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him, and the Greek epithet ο Ομολογητής matches the folder's Romanian «Isihie Mărturisitorul». **The page carries no life at all and says where the life is**: «Η μνήμη του Οσίου Ησυχίου του Ομολογητού τιμάται την 6η Μαρτίου, όπου και ο βίος του.» So there is a second Greek day for him, and it is recorded here as a note and not as a second row: one attestation row per church is the schema, and the row records the day page read. **Two things a writer should see, and neither is decided here.** First, saint.gr's 6 Μαρτίου listing does not print this epithet: it prints «Όσιος Ησύχιος ο Θαυματουργός», the Wonderworker, and the settled rule is that two entries on one calendar are two commemorations, so the redirect may point at a page for another man of the name. Second, 6 Μαρτίου has already been read for this wave and its drafts contain no Hesychius at all, so no row of that day's is displaced by this one. Both are named in the report. **`dates` stay absent**: the page gives no year, and the 6 Μαρτίου page was not opened by this reader. **No hymn** is on the 10 Μαΐου page. The only other thing it prints is the distich: «Τὸν βίον Ἡσύχιος ἄγων ἡσύχως, / Ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ πρὸς Θεὸν διαβαίνει».
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).
